newsitem.title: POLAND: Lithuania, Poland, Ukraine speak out on Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania, Poland, Ukraine speak out on Belarus.

text.p: The presidents of Lithuania, Ukraine and Poland issued a joint declaration on Wednesday calling for a constitutional resolution of the political conflict in Belarus and for human rights to be respected there.
In a statement issued by the office of Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski, the presidents said: "We hereby express our deep concern over the developments in the Republic of Belarus."
They said they were acting as neighbours of Belarus, guided by concern for its future and fully respecting its sovereignty.

"We call for a constitutional resolution of the present conflict and for respect for human rights and civil liberties, in compliance with universally accepted international standards and universal principles of democracy," it said.
The statement was signed by Kwasniewski, Lithuania's Algirdas Brazauskas and Ukraine's Leonid Kuczma.
The presidents said good relations between the countries in the region constituted a significant contribution to stability, peace and prosperity in Europe.
Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko has clashed with parliament over his plans to increase his powers through a referendum on November 24.

On Wednesday Lukashenko rebuffed pressure from Russia to attend peace talks in the Russian city of Smolensk, which were intended to defuse mounting tension in the former Soviet republic of 10 million people.
Poland, Lithuania and Ukraine hope to avoid political instability in the region as they try to forge closer links with the West and build up their economies.

Poland expects to be one of the first countries to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation before the end of the century. It considers one of its responsibilities to be the cultivation of good relations with its neighbours, partly to avoid a new fault-line across Europe.
